before.permit: North Cascades NP complex: no permit for day climbs; all overnight backcountry stays require a backcountry permit (reserve on Recreation.gov or walk-up at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center).

access.fees: $10 per person (charged mid-May through early October; no fee October-mid-May) plus a $6 non-refundable processing fee — applies to advance reservations, lottery entries, and walk-up/first-come-first-served permits alike, not just reservations; youth 15 and under free.
access.notes: 60% of sites are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.rules: Group size capped at 6 in off-trail cross-country zones (which includes most Picket Range approaches; 12 in on-trail corridors). Bear canisters required in some zones — free loaners at permit offices.
access.permit: NPS backcountry permit required year-round for overnight stays. About 60% of sites can be reserved in advance via Recreation.gov (watch the mandatory safety video, then email noca_wilderness@nps.gov within 3 days of the trip); the rest are held as walk-up/standby permits issued in person at the Wilderness Information Center, 7280 Ranger Station Rd, Marblemount, WA, (360) 854-7245.
access.closures: SR 20 (North Cascades Highway) itself closes seasonally, but the gate is well east of here near Ross Dam/Diablo (roughly late November-late April, varying with snowpack and any slide repairs). Newhalem and the Goodell Creek trailhead sit west of that gate and remain reachable year-round from Marblemount/Concrete.

waypoints.name: Goodell Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: Old Goodell Creek logging road on SR 20 across from Newhalem Campground; free NPS backcountry permit required for any overnight camping in North Cascades National Park.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to Newhalem. Coming from the west through Marblemount and Concrete the road is open year-round, since the seasonal highway closure gate sits farther east near Ross Dam and Diablo. Park at the Goodell Creek trailhead on the north side of SR-20, across from Newhalem Campground: take the left just past the Goodell Creek crossing, continue past the gravel pit, and follow the road to its end by the creek at about 500 ft. Any overnight camping in North Cascades National Park needs a free backcountry wilderness permit, and the Crescent/Terror Creek approach is usually not snow-free and reliably passable until mid-to-late July.

waypoints.name: Climbers' Path Cairn
waypoints.note: Cairn marking where the unmaintained Terror Basin/Barrier climbers' path leaves the overgrown Goodell Creek roadbed and turns steeply uphill toward the Southern Pickets.

waypoints.name: Terror Creek Log Crossing
waypoints.note: Cross Terror Creek on a large logjam ford point used by climbers approaching the Barrier; can be slick and the log position shifts year to year.

waypoints.name: The Barrier Crest
waypoints.note: Small saddle atop a notoriously loose class-3 ridge dividing the Terror and Crescent Creek basins; careful route-finding and rockfall awareness needed here.

waypoints.name: Stump Hollow
waypoints.note: Open, gentle slabby/heather basin between the Barrier and Chopping Block ridge — the standard high camp for the South Route.

waypoints.name: South Face Gully
waypoints.note: Loose gully on the south side of the Chopping Block/Barrier ridge gains the sloping south face; helmet on, watch for rockfall onto climbers below.

waypoints.name: The Chopping Block
waypoints.note: True summit (6,819 ft), labeled Pinnacle Peak on USGS maps; visible from the North Cascades NP Newhalem visitor center on clear days.

itinerary.cal: North Cascades NP backcountry camping requires a wilderness permit, and the Crescent/Terror Creek approach is typically not snow-free and reliably passable until mid-to-late July.

days.note: From the Goodell Creek trailhead near Newhalem, follow the old logging road then a steep, sometimes brushy climbers' path south of Terror Creek (wading the creek), climbing relentlessly to a ~6,200 ft spur on the Barrier ridge before dropping to a flat camp around 5,800 ft. It's a brutal, sustained ~4,000+ ft grind with little flat ground until camp.
days.title: Approach to Southern Pickets high camp
days.objective: Reach camp near the Barrier / Terror Basin

days.note: Cross the Barrier ridge into Stump Hollow/Crescent Creek Basin, then climb south-side slabs and heather to the base of the peak. The route is a rambly scramble with a couple of short, exposed low-5th-class moves near the summit plateau; parties typically make one short rappel (fixed-line/anchor reported at the top) to regain the south-side ledges on descent rather than down-climbing the exposed step. Often combined with an adjacent objective (e.g. West Ridge of Terror) on the same day if time and conditions allow.
days.title: Chopping Block summit via South Route

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start, cross the Barrier toward Stump Hollow/Crescent Creek Basin.

schedule.label: Reach base of south side
schedule.detail: Traverse slabs/heather below the Chopping Block's south aspect.

schedule.label: Scramble to summit plateau
schedule.detail: Low 5th-class moves near the top; stay near the east side to avoid the hardest ground.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Short rappel down the south side to regain scramble ledges.

days.objective: Climb the Chopping Block and return to camp

days.note: Reverse the approach: climb back over the Barrier spur and descend the steep climbers' path to Terror Creek and the old logging road back to the car. Loose scree/dirt and brush make the descent slow and hard on the knees despite being downhill.
days.title: Descend to Goodell Creek trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day Southern Pickets trip (~6.5 mi and ~5,700 ft each way to camp); the Chopping Block itself is a moderate scramble/rappel day out of high camp and is commonly tacked on as a warm-up alongside another Southern Pickets objective.

access.fees: $10 per person backcountry recreation fee plus a $6 nonrefundable permit/reservation fee — applies to advance Recreation.gov reservations, early-access lottery entries, and walk-up permits alike; no charge for youth 15 and under. This per-person structure replaced the former flat ~$20–26 per-permit fee in March 2024.
access.notes: The Southern Pickets cross-country zones (Terror Basin and Crescent Creek) cannot be reserved in advance; permits are walk-up only, issued in person at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount the day of or the day before the trip.
access.rules: Camp only within the cross-country zone written on your permit.
access.permit: NPS backcountry permit required for any overnight stay ($10/person/night + $6 nonrefundable fee as of March 2024 — no longer free).
